newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India issues one-year term tenders to buy diesel.
newsitem.headline: India issues one-year term tenders to buy diesel.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has issued three one-year term tenders for the purchase of high speed diesel for delivery from June 1997 to May 1998, traders said on Wednesday.
The first tender seeks 12 cargoes of 40,000-45,0000 tonne each of 0.25 percent sulphur diesel for delivery to Kandla on the west coast.
The second tender seeks 12 cargoes of 40,000-45,000 tonnes each of 1.0 percent diesel for delivery to Kandla and to Madras, Haldia or Vizag on the Indian east coast.
The third tender seeks 12 cargoes cargoes each of 87,000-tonnes and/ or 130,000 tonnes of 1.0 percent diesel for delivery to Kandla.
Deliveries have to be between 1-7 and/or 16-23 of each month.
The tender closes on April 29 and offers will be valid until May 3.
Last month IOC declined to accept any offers for its initial term tender to buy diesel for delivery from May 1997 to April 1998.
Traders said IOC usually issues an initial tender to get a feel for the market as was the case last year.
In its last one-year term contract IOC bought one cargo each from western trading house Cargill, Swiss trader Glencore and Dutch Trader Vitol. That contract started from July 1996.
